Delivered total revenues in Q3 2026 of approximately $3.66 billion, exceeding guidance of $3.3 billion while growing 58.5%, the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO.

In partnership with AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft, and Qualcomm, Arista launched open standards-based rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI networks.

In September 2026, Arista was added to the S&P 100, an index comprised of 100 major blue-chip companies across multiple industry groups.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., November 03, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"Arista registered another momentous quarter with the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO and record profitability, surpassing even my high expectations," stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. "This strong momentum across customer sectors highlights our increased relevance for the generative and agentic AI era."

Third Quarter Financial Highlights

Revenue of $3.66 billion, an increase of 20.5% compared to the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of 58.5% from the third quarter of 2025.

GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.9% and 49.1%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 42.4% and 48.6% in the third quarter of 2025.

GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.22 and $1.20, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.67 and $0.77 in the third quarter of 2025.

A reconciliation of the company's non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release.

Commenting on the company's financial performance, Chantelle Breithaupt, CFO, said, "This quarter brought a true trifecta for our company, setting new record highs in revenue growth, net income, and EPS. I'm incredibly proud of the Arista team for their hard work in driving such outstanding performance for our shareholders."

Company Highlights

Arista announced open Ethernet rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics – The new liquid-cooled portfolio leverages Ethernet for Scale-Up Networks (ESUN) and introduces the Etherlink™ SU-144 architecture, supporting up to 144 accelerators per rack in a single hop and scaling up to 1,024 XPUs via cross-rack topologies.

Arista detailed its scale-across networking strategy for distributed AI fabrics – Highlighting the flagship Arista 7800 AI Spine and unified Arista EOS®, the company outlined how Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) multiplane forwarding, deterministic routing, and real-time congestion signaling enable lossless, high-radix AI fabrics across geographically distributed data centers up to one million XPUs.

Arista expanded AI-driven software security across its development lifecycle – Collaborating with the likes of Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, Arista embedded domain-specific AI harnesses that accelerate proactive vulnerability discovery, building on the company's track record of low CVEs and no-downtime upgrades.

title: Hyperscalers Face “$1.5 Trillion Gap” Between AI Spending and Cash
detail:
Hyperscalers Face “$1.5 Trillion Gap” Between AI Spending and Cash
Roxanna Maglangit

MSFT

AMZN
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Hyperscalers Face "$1.5 Trillion Gap" Between AI Spending and Cash ©Natee Meepian's Images and Yuganov Konstantin via Canva
Key Takeaways

Hyperscaler free cash flow turned negative in the third quarter for the first time, and Microsoft is the only one of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms and Oracle with positive free cash flow.

Prof G Markets co-host Ed Elson expects the five companies to spend more than $2 trillion on capex over the next two years, against nearly $600 billion of cash on hand.

His $1.5 trillion figure leaves out the cash these companies' operations still bring in, but spending is growing much faster than that cash, and Meta and Alphabet are already turning to stock and bond buyers.

Microsoft still pays for its buildout from operations, so it's the best placed of the five if investors get less willing to fund the rest.

Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOG), Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ), Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) and Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) are spending so much on AI data centers that, as a group, they can no longer pay for it out of their own cash flow.

Carson Group's Ryan Detrick flagged it on X on Monday, citing his colleague Sonu Varghese: "Hyperscaler free cash flow turned negative for the first time ever in Q3."

On Monday's episode of Prof G Markets, co-host Ed Elson put a dollar figure on what that means. He expects the five companies' capex over the next two years to be more than $2 trillion. He counts nearly $600 billion of cash and short-term investments among them, including more than $120 billion at Amazon and more than $250 billion at Alphabet. That leaves, in his words, "a one and a half trillion dollar gap between how much money they're going to spend and how much money they actually have."

That's a lot of money to ask investors for.

TIKR tracks 57 analysts on Microsoft. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Microsoft, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Microsoft's Analyst Ratings

Smaller than $1.5 trillion, and growing fast

Elson's math leaves out one big thing: the cash these businesses still bring in from operations, which pays for most of the spending today. Negative free cash flow means the spending has moved ahead of that cash. The cash is still coming in.

Meta shows it clearly. Its capex has climbed until, in the September quarter, it was more than the cash its operations brought in:

Meta Platforms (META): cash from operations vs. capital expenditures, $ billions, last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)

Meta's capex rose 80% from a year earlier, to $33.9 billion, while its operating cash rose 9%, to $32.8 billion. That's the real gap, and it grows every quarter that spending rises faster than cash. Elson expects capex to keep rising next year and the year after, so the gap could get big quickly. By his count, Oracle, Amazon and Alphabet are already in negative free cash flow too.
